==English== ===Pronunciation=== * {{enPR|wēv}}, {{IPA|en|/wiːv/}} * {{audio|en|en-us-weave.ogg|a=US}} * {{homophones|en|we've}} * {{rhymes|en|iːv|s=1}} ===Etymology 1=== From {{inh|en|enm|weven|t=to weave|id=to weave}}, from {{inh|en|ang|wefan||to weave}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*weban}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*webaną}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*webʰ-||to weave, braid}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|frr|weev}}, {{m|frr|weew}}, {{m|frr|weewe|t=to weave}}, {{cog|stq|weeuwe|t=to weave}}, {{cog|nl|weven|t=to weave}}, {{cog|de|weben|t=to weave}}, {{cog|lb|wiewen|t=to weave}}, {{cog|yi|וועבן|t=to weave}}, {{cog|da|væve|t=to weave}}, {{cog|fo|veva|t=to weave}}, {{cog|is|vefa|t=to weave}}, {{cog|nb|veve|t=to weave}}, {{cog|nn|veva}}, {{m|nn|veve|t=to weave}}, {{cog|sv|väva|t=to weave}}. {{col-bottom}} ====Verb==== {{en-verb|+|+|wove,~d|woven,~d,wove}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[form]] something by [[pass]]ing [[length]]s or [[strand]]s of [[material]] over and under one another. #: {{ux|en|This loom '''weaves''' yarn into cloth.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|journal=Handwoven|year=2026|volume=XLVII|number=1|page=80|title='''Weaving''' with Aloha|author=Rebecca Fox |text=Eugene "Uncle Onio" Punzal has lived on Kauai his whole life. He began '''weaving''' coconut fronds when he was a young child after seeing traditional weavers selling their pāpales (a traditional style of crownless hat) and baskets to tourists on the beach.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[spin]] a [[cocoon]] or a [[web]]. #: {{ux|en|Spiders '''weave''' beautiful but deadly webs.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[unite]] by close [[connection]] or [[intermixture]]. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare King Lear|II|i|passage=This '''weaves''' itself, perforce, into my business.}} #* {{RQ:Byron Childe Harold|canto=III|stanza=CII|passage=these words, thus '''woven''' into song}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[compose]] [[creative]]ly and [[intricate]]ly; to [[fabricate]]. #: {{ux|en|to '''weave''' the plot of a story}} =====Related terms===== * {{l|en|web}} * {{l|en|sew}} History of Textiles|author=Kax Wilson|publisher=Westview Press|year=1979|ISBN=0891584919|page=239 |text=Although fabrics of complex '''weave''' can most surely be identified as being imports, others, Li; Howard I. Maibach|title=Ethnic Skin and Hair and Other Cultural Considerations|page=154 |passage=The physician should evaluate for a history of tight ponytails, buns, chignons, braids, twists, '''weaves''', cornrows, dreadlocks, sisterlocks, and hair wefts in addition to the usage of religious hair coverings.}} =====Translations===== {{trans-top|a type or way of weaving}} * Bulgarian: * Chinese: * Dutch: * Finnish: * French: * German: * Greek: * Hindi: * Irish: * Italian: * Japanese: * Kurdish: * Macedonian: * Norwegian: * Portuguese: * Serbo-Croatian: * Spanish: * Swedish: * Tagalog: * Telugu: * Welsh: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|human or artificial hair worn}} * Bulgarian: * Finnish: * Macedonian: * Portuguese: {{trans-bottom}} ====Derived terms==== {{col|en|basketweave|even-weave|mana weave|Panama weave|plain weave|satin weave|Thach weave|what a tangled web we weave when first we practice to deceive|evenweave|flatweave|folkweave|interweave|inweave|misweave|outweave|reweave|unweave|weavable|weavy|weft}} ===Etymology 2=== From {{inh|en|enm|weven|t=to wander|id=to wander}}; probably from {{der|en|non|veifa||move around, wave}}, related to Latin {{m|la|vibrare}}. ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To move by [[turn]]ing and [[twist]]ing. #: {{ux|en|The drunk '''weaved''' into another bar.}} #* {{RQ:Observer|date=August 20, 2017| title=The Observer view on the attacks in Spain| url=https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2017/aug/19/observer-view-on-spain-attacks-united-europe-can-act-to-foil-terrorism| passage=The victims’ feeling of incredulity at what they were seeing, swiftly turning to paralysing fear as the van bore down on them, swerving and '''weaving''' to hit as many people as possible, can barely be imagined.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261013070951/https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2017/aug/19/observer-view-on-spain-attacks-united-europe-can-act-to-foil-terrorism|archivedate=13 October 2026}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To make (a path or way) by [[wind]]ing in and out or from side to side. #: {{ux|en|The ambulance '''weaved''' its way through the heavy traffic.}} #* {{RQ:Coleridge Christabel|page=58|passage='''Weave''' a circle round him thrice,
And close your eyes with holy dread:
For he on honey-dew hath fed,
And drank the milk of Paradise.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|of an animal}} To move the head back and forth in a [[stereotyped]] pattern, typically as a symptom of stress. =====Translations===== {{trans-top-see|to move by turning and twisting|dodge}} * Albanian: * Bulgarian: * Finnish: * French: * Japanese: * Māori: * Norwegian: * Russian: {{t+|ru|заворачивать|impf}} * Slovene: * Spanish: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|to make (a path or way) by winding in and out or from side to side}} * Bulgarian: * French: * Māori: * Portuguese: * Vietnamese: {{trans-bottom}} ====References==== * {{R:Century}} * {{R:Webster 1913}} {{cln|en|strong verbs|irregular verbs}} {{C|en|Hair|Weaving}}
